newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Brokers sign off on PNG's Highlands Pacific float.
newsitem.headline: Brokers sign off on PNG's Highlands Pacific float.

text.p: Papua New Guinea (PNG) resource group Highlands Pacific Ltd has completed an underwriting agreement with brokers Merill Lynch and Wilson HTM, a spokesman from Wilson HTM said on Wednesday.

"The underwriting was signed, as we indicated it would be, yesterday late in the day. We are proceeding with getting the prospectus registered in PNG and Australia as quickly as possible," David Cleary, Wilson HTM director of corporate services, told Reuters.
Cleary said the offer was due to open on April 21 and close in mid-May and the company expected to list on the Australian Stock Exchange in the first or second week of June.
Highlands Pacific was born from a restructure proposal put forward by Highlands Gold Ltd following a takeover offer by Canadian miner Placer Dome Inc late last year.
Under the plan, Placer Dome would control Highland Gold's 25 percent stake in the Porgera gold mine in PNG, while Highlands Pacific would buy the group's remaining assets in PNG and Indonesia.
Placer won control of Highlands Gold with a 75 cent a share offer and Highlands Gold shareholders would recieve a three-for-10 entitlement in the new company.
Highlands Gold has said a consortium of PNG institutions had strongly supported the restructuring and were expected to invest up to A$110 million in the float.
Highlands Gold has previously stated the Highlands Pacific float would raise A$190 million through the issue of 190 million shares at A$1 each.
